title: Jason Cohen: Why founders burn out, and how to build a company that doesn't need you
summary: Jason Cohen uses an anonymous burned-out founder's post to argue that founders must make emotionally difficult choices early. Fire fast, hire people better than you and manage them by results, and place yourself where what you like, what you're good at and what the company needs overlap. He draws on selling SmartBear and handing the CEO role at WP Engine to Heather Bruner.

principles.text: If you can't stop thinking about a decision at 2am, you're avoiding the hard choice. Take action.
principles.quote: when you wake up at 2:00 in the morning you're like oh no ha like that that simple thing not a deep analysis just that simple thing if I can't stop thinking about how this person's here and they shouldn't be that indicates you do need to take action

principles.text: Make hard calls like firing quickly, because delay hurts everyone. Be decisive, then kind.
principles.quote: General Patton on the decision mother Teresa on the exit be decisive and then be kind that's the right way to do it

principles.text: You can't become an expert in an entire career's worth of work in a few months. Hire A players for functions you don't know.
principles.quote: the idea that you can become an expert in something important something that's an entire career for someone else in a few months and then hiring a player that's of course not true so you're actually a C player at best

principles.text: Hire results-oriented people and manage them on outcomes, since you can't tell them how to do a job you don't know.
principles.quote: you have to manage the results of it and hold them to that bar so by hiring for people who are already think that way already like to be measured by the results that they make instead of what they do then that's how you're gonna manage them

principles.text: Aim for a strong, resilient organization in which people are better than you and the company doesn't depend on the founder.
principles.quote: if you can agree that the best thing is to have everyone in the organization be better than you then you can create a resilient organization

principles.text: Choose your role at the overlap of what you like, what you're good at and what the company needs. Don't do needed work you dislike, find someone who loves it.
principles.quote: what the company needed and what I liked not to mention what I was good at did not mix I like product and engineering so I went and became the CTO
